rule.title: Semantic HTML and ARIA Labeling on Interactive Elements
rule.statement: Interactive elements must use semantic HTML tags (<button>, <a>, <input>) and provide explicit aria-label attributes when icons lack text labels.
rule.rationale: Using <div onClick=...> prevents screen readers from announcing elements as interactive and disables keyboard activation via Space and Enter.

source.chapter: Chapter 11: UI Systems and Atomic Design
source.evidence_quote: Use native semantic HTML elements whenever possible. They provide built-in keyboard navigation and screen reader semantics that custom div containers lack.

rule.title: Fitts's Law: Minimum Target Size of 44x44px for Interactive Elements
rule.statement: Interactive touch and click targets (buttons, icon buttons, checkboxes) must have an effective hit area of at least 44x44 CSS pixels with adequate spacing.
rule.rationale: Small, cramped targets increase acquisition time and cause accidental misclicks, particularly on mobile touchscreens or high-DPI displays.
rule.implementation_guidance: For small visual icons (16px), add padding or an invisible bounding box to ensure the clickable area reaches at least 44px (min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]).

forbidden.example: <button className="h-4 w-4 p-0"><XIcon className="h-4 w-4" /></button> // Extremely difficult to click

preferred.example: <button className="p-3 min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] flex items-center justify-center"><XIcon className="h-4 w-4" /></button>

source.evidence_quote: The time to acquire a target is a function of the distance to and size of the target. Touch targets should be large enough (at least 44 × 44 pt) and have sufficient spacing.
